intro: Most of what you say in a day happens in the present: I work, you eat, we live here, they are coming. In Spanish, each of those ideas lives inside one verb whose ending tells you who is acting. *Hablo* (I speak), hablas (you speak), hablamos (we speak). Once you see how stems and endings fit together, thousands of regular verbs open up at once.

This unit follows two families. One runs a taquería and uses regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs all week long. The other packs for a trip to Guadalajara and runs into the irregular verbs every speaker needs, like tengo, hago, voy and sé. Along the way you will learn when to use saber or conocer and how to talk about plans with ir a plus an infinitive.

By the end, you will be able to conjugate any regular verb, recognize vosotros and ustedes, use the most common irregular yo forms, and describe your week and your weekend plans in clear, correct Spanish. Heritage speakers will get names for patterns they already use; new learners will get a system they can trust.
bigQuestion: How does the present tense let you describe your life, your habits and your plans in Spanish?

words.d: the infinitive — the base form of a verb, ending in -ar, -er or -ir
the stem — what is left after you drop -ar, -er or -ir
to conjugate — to change the verb ending to match the subject
you all — used for any group in Latin America
you all (informal) — used mainly in Spain
never — goes before the verb, or after it with no
to do or make — yo hago
to know facts or how to do something — yo sé
to know people or places, or to meet — yo conozco
going to + verb — the near future: Voy a comer.

test.q: Choose the correct form: Tú ___ muy bien. (cocinar)
Choose the correct form: Nosotros ___ cartas. (escribir)
Choose the correct form: Ellas ___ agua. (beber)
Which pronoun is used mainly in Spain for "you all" among friends?
test.why: Vosotros is the informal plural you, used mainly in Spain.

test.q: Choose the correct form: Usted ___ en Chicago. (vivir)
test.why: Usted uses the él ending: vive.
Nunca goes before the conjugated verb.

test.q: Choose the correct form: Yo ___ de casa a las siete. (salir)
test.why: Salir is a yo-go verb: salgo.

test.q: Choose the correct form: Ella ___ dos hermanos. (tener)
test.why: Tener changes e to ie for ella: tiene.

test.q: Choose the correct form: Yo ___ un regalo a mi mamá. (dar)
test.why: Dar has the irregular yo form doy.

test.q: Choose the correct verb: ¿___ a mi prima Lucía?
test.why: Knowing a person uses conocer; tú takes conoces.

test.q: Choose the correct verb: No ___ dónde está el hotel.
test.why: Where something is counts as information, so use saber: sé.
Ir a + infinitive: voy a estudiar.

test.q: What does "Siempre trabajamos los sábados" mean?
choices: We are going to work Saturday.
test.why: Siempre means always, trabajamos is nosotros, and los sábados is a weekly habit.

test.q: Which sentence uses a + el correctly?
test.why: A + el always joins as al.

test.q: Why can you say "Hablo español" without yo?
choices: yo is never used in Spanish
test.why: In the present, the -o ending of a regular verb shows the subject is yo.

write.prompt: Escribe un párrafo sobre tu semana y tus planes. Write one paragraph in Spanish (6–8 sentences): describe three things you do every week (use regular verbs and siempre, a veces or nunca), one thing you know or know how to do (sé or conozco), and three plans for this weekend (voy a + infinitive).
tips: Use verbs from this unit: trabajar, comer, vivir, hacer, salir, tener, ir.
Check every ending against the subject: -o for yo, -amos, -emos or -imos for nosotros.
Remember the irregular yo forms: hago, salgo, tengo, conozco, sé, voy.
In ir a + infinitive, change only ir; the second verb stays as it is.
Read your paragraph aloud to hear any ending that sounds wrong.
